name: PT Chandra Daya Investasi TBK.

frontmatter.title: Chandra Daya Investasi: one balance-sheet date, a corrected peer set, and a wider premium
frontmatter.summary: We rebuilt the valuation on a single 30 September balance sheet, took the Barito sibling out of the peer set so no regime premium enters fundamental value, and charged the fourth quarter at nine-month cost and depreciation rates. Fundamental value falls, the price-to-value gap widens, and the target is Rp259 against Rp330 - REDUCE.
thesis: Four infrastructure pillars inside the Chandra Asri group: electricity distribution in the Krakatau industrial estate, water, tank and jetty storage, and marine and land logistics [S4, S5].

The nine-month result splits the story: time charter revenue reached US$40.0m, already above the US$34.6m earned in all of FY2025, while electricity and tank rental fell; the growth is real but concentrated in the least visible pillar [S17, S4].
Reported profit fell 61.5% because the prior year's one-off other gain of US$45.4m did not repeat - this year's line was US$3.5m - and finance costs rose to US$40.2m [S17].

A large related-party financial portfolio - parent-issued equity-linked bonds, quoted shares and a loan to CAP subsidiaries - carries almost all of book equity and must be valued separately from the operations [S4, S17].

Leverage is the binding constraint: nine-month finance costs exceed the operating result, operating cash flow is negative, and debt of US$894.3m carries US$272.2m due in 2031 with US$90.0m of AMP subscription still to fund [S17, S2].

The shares trade at 3.1x our fundamental value; the premium is a float and regime variable, and the March 2027 free-float step plus the June 2027 MSCI decision are the dated forces that should compress part of it [S10, S8, S11].

catalysts.event: First free-float deadline for large caps below the intermediate threshold, to the intermediate step [S8]
End of the MSCI consultation feedback period on Standalone status for Indonesia [S11]
MSCI decision on the Standalone proposal [S11]
Target commercial operation of the port and storage projects funded from the IPO proceeds [S14]
Final free-float deadline for large caps below the intermediate threshold, to the full minimum [S8]

blocks.text: What changed. Three valuation changes. The bridge now sits on one balance-sheet date - net debt, associates, minorities and portfolio all at 30 September 2026, not June debt against September assets [S17, S2]. The peer set drops the Barito sibling whose own konglo premium would have entered fundamental value before the lens applies the regime again, so the EV/EBITDA median falls. And the fourth quarter is charged at the nine-month cost and depreciation rates the filing shows [S17, S4]. Fundamental value is Rp115 against Rp330; the target Rp259, a return of -21.0%, rating REDUCE [S2, S0].

The business, unchanged. Revenue rose to US$122.0m from US$104.8m, up 16.0%, while net profit fell to US$32.2m from US$83.5m, down 61.5% [S17, S14]. Financial-asset income was flat at US$16.8m; the swing is the one-off other gain, US$45.4m against US$3.5m, plus finance costs of US$40.2m [S17].

Management's EBITDA needs care. It reports US$49.9m, up 65.0%, a 41.0% margin [S14]; on our definition the margin is about half, because the figure includes associate income of US$10.5m and the foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m [S17]. The fair-value line of US$16.8m sits below the operating line, in neither figure.

The premium is the story. The price is 3.1x today's fundamental value of Rp105. The base regime closes 35.0% of the log gap over twelve months and gives Rp241; the bear gives Rp153 and the bull Rp403, twenty-two per cent above today's price. The probability-weighted target of Rp259 gives a return of -21.0%, so the REDUCE rests on the weighting - half the mass on the base, a quarter on the bear - not on a bull case that loses money [S2, S10, S0].

CDIA reports four segments: energy, logistics, tank and jetty rental, and other services. Electricity earned US$67.1m, time charter US$40.0m, fuel sales US$8.3m, tank and jetty rental US$3.7m and warehouse rental US$1.5m, with other services the balance [S17]. Energy is close to two thirds of revenue but fell year on year, while time charter in nine months beat the US$34.6m earned in all of FY2025 [S17].

Energy earned US$12.2m of segment result and logistics US$10.4m, so the smaller half of revenue now earns nearly as much as the larger half [S17]. The energy pillar runs a gas and steam combined-cycle plant of 120 MW serving the Krakatau industrial estate and about 311 electricity customers, and holds an interest in an associate operating a 200 MW coal-fired plant [S5].

Management says more than nine tenths of revenue is contract-based, but the filing's related-party share is 23.2% of nine-month revenue, up from 17.2%, with CAP at US$12.8m the only customer above a tenth [S14, S17]. CAP holds 60.0%, Phoenix Power B.V. 30.0%, the public 10.0% and the company 79.5m treasury shares [S2, S17].

In electricity CDIA is the incumbent distributor inside the Krakatau industrial estate, buying bulk power and gas and reselling to tenants under long-term arrangements; in logistics and storage it is a challenger in a fragmented market [S5, S9]. The moat is the estate - duplicating substations, water treatment and jetty access makes little sense - and it does not extend into shipping, where charter rates are competitive [S5]. Supplier power is high because the state utility supplies the bulk power; entry barriers are the concession and the capital for tanks and vessels [S4].

The regulation that matters most is capital-markets: large caps below the intermediate threshold must reach the intermediate float step by end-March 2027 and the full minimum a year later [S8], OJK has kept an exit-policy option [S7], and MSCI's Standalone consultation, decided by June 2027, points the other way at passive outflows [S11].
Growth is a function of Krakatau industrial demand, because new tenants bring electricity, water and logistics volume together, and the current build is tanks, storage and ports [S5, S9, S14].

Revenue rose to US$122.0m in the nine months from US$104.8m, leaving gross profit of US$25.6m against US$24.0m [S17]. All the growth came from logistics: electricity slipped to US$67.1m and tank and jetty rental to US$3.7m [S17, S4].

Our EBITDA is rebuilt from the filing: depreciation was US$14.9m in the nine months alone, against US$9.6m in FY2025 and US$8.6m in FY2024 [S17, S4]. On that basis nine-month operating EBITDA is about half of management's US$49.9m, the gap being associate income of US$10.5m and the foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m [S17]. The fair-value income of US$16.8m is a portfolio mark in neither figure.

The fourth quarter uses nine-month rates: revenue of US$122.0m against FY2026E of US$167.3m leaves a seasonally strong quarter at operating costs of 11.8% of revenue and depreciation of 12.2% [S17], where the earlier build used 10.0% and a fourth-quarter margin above every reported quarter on a flat-to-down gross margin. FY2026E EBITDA is US$37.5m at a 22.4% margin, in line with the third quarter [S17, S0].

Interest is where the model and the run-rate diverge. FY2026E finance costs are US$39.4m, charged on opening debt at the 7.0% marginal rate, while the nine months already cost US$40.2m on debt that reached US$894.3m by September [S17, S2]. On closing debt throughout the full-year charge would be the FY2027E figure of US$62.6m, which matters against FY2026E parent profit of US$21.3m; the yield check below uses a token distribution a fuller charge would reduce rather than increase.

The profit line carries the quality question. Profit before tax was US$44.5m against US$12.4m of tax, leaving US$32.2m for the group [S17]. Below the operating line sat finance income of US$29.9m, fair-value income of US$16.8m, associate income of US$10.5m, a foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m and other gains of US$3.5m, against finance costs of US$40.2m [S17]. FY2026E profit of US$22.5m sits below the nine months because the model forecasts neither the gain nor the full fair-value income.

The AMP subscription is the new cash commitment: 40.0% of PT Armada Maritim Persada for US$90.0m, of which US$30.0m was paid and US$31.0m is carried as an associate [S17]. The balance converts into an asset at cost, so it is not a bridge claim, but it is a cash call on the same bank lines as the capex [S17, S13].

Net cash used in operations was US$6.3m, against US$7.7m provided a year earlier, while capex was US$121.3m and the related-party loan absorbed US$235.0m [S17]. Dividends of US$50.0m, a US$4.6m buyback and new bank loans lifted debt to US$894.3m from US$562.6m; cash rose to US$485.9m [S17]. The portfolio - US$358.1m of bonds, US$230.3m of quoted shares, a US$245.2m loan to CAP subsidiaries and US$205.1m of associates - exceeds gross debt and is close to the whole of book equity [S17].

Leverage, correctly stated. The model's FY2026E net debt/EBITDA of 6.8x is not the filing's: its cash line of US$639.8m exceeds the US$485.9m reported at 30 September because the roll omits the US$235.0m related-party loan and charges US$58.8m of dividends against US$50.0m paid [S2, S17]. On the filing's balances, US$894.3m of debt less US$485.9m of cash over FY2026E EBITDA of US$37.5m is ten point nine times, against the model's 6.8x; the risk section uses the filing basis [S17, S2].

Earnings-quality flags. Fair value is a mark, not cash; related-party revenue is 23.2% of the total, up from 17.2%; the largest financial asset is paper issued by the controlling shareholder's listed vehicle; and management's EBITDA is not reconciled to operating profit [S17, S4, S14]. On accruals, profit of US$32.2m against an operating outflow of US$6.3m on average assets of US$2,066.0m and US$1,743.8m a year earlier is a low single-digit ratio, inside the card's alarm level, though the trend has turned from covered to negative [S17]. These are optics-class, not manipulation-class.

The forecast holds the last actual's economics. Revenue grows 13.0% in FY2026E, fading to 8.0%; the post-depreciation gross margin is 22.0%, rising to the FY2025 level as the fleet annualises; capex is 85.0% of revenue, fading to a reinvestment rate above depreciation; operating EBIT is taxed at 22.0% and net borrowing of US$331.7m reflects the actual nine-month increase [S17, S4, S9].

We value CDIA on the house power-utilities method set: DCF 60%, EV/EBITDA cross-check 30% and dividend-yield check 10%; P/E is dropped: it would capitalise the FY2025 fair-value gain and FVTPL marks [S4, S17]. Long-dated estate and tank contracts and non-operating income in reported multiples make the DCF primary at Rp96 a share [S4, S17].

The cost of capital is the house build: a rupiah risk-free rate of 4.9%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and the house unlevered beta of 0.60, levered to 0.78, giving a cost of equity of 10.1%, a WACC of 8.8% and a cost of debt of 6.9% [S4, S2]. The registry beta of 1.99 describes a year in which the shares fell from Rp2,050 to Rp330, not operating risk, and gearing uses that same 3.1x-of-value price, so WACC is understated and the DCF flattered [S10, S0].

The DCF gives an enterprise value of US$106.1m, 123.4% of it terminal because the explicit years are cash-negative [S2, S17]. The bridge sits entirely at 30 September 2026: portfolio US$358.1m, related-party loan US$245.2m, quoted shares US$230.3m and associates US$205.1m, against net debt of US$894.3m less US$485.9m and minorities of US$74.6m [S17]. The earlier version carried June debt and a June cash line predating the US$235.0m loan against September assets. Moving all four legs together cuts bridge equity by a small percentage of value, since the portfolio rise offsets most of the debt rise, but one date is the only consistent mark [S17, S2].

The terminal assumptions are house constructs, not company disclosures, and with 123.4% of the value in the terminal period they are load-bearing: the long-run capex rate is set at a reinvestment rate above depreciation and the long-run opex ratio at 10.0%. We tested both on the engine: one percentage point on either moves the DCF by roughly a twentieth - the capex rate to about ninety-one rupiah a share and the opex ratio to about ninety-two, against Rp96 - so the sensitivity is symmetric and neither flips the rating. The
grid shows the WACC and terminal-growth axes the engine computes.

Three holdings need the recovery test. The related-party loan is US$245.2m, three loans to CAP subsidiaries at a 12.0% coupon maturing on 30 November 2035, with no impairment provision disclosed and the coupon received; we carry it at face, the filing's basis [S2, S17]. The US$326.4m equity-linked bond, inside the US$358.1m portfolio of other financial assets, is at fair value and carries a 51.0% option over CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary; the option is inside the mark, since the LK discloses neither strike nor exercise terms, so nothing separate is added [S2]. The associates of US$205.1m include KPE at US$79.3m [S2]. The annual report's US$200.0m is the stake at acquisition and the top-up cost US$46.4m the top of the range [S5]; capitalising KPE's US$2.4m half-year profit share at the cost of equity gives only about sixty per cent of the US$79.3m carrying value, so book is carried as the filing basis with the acquisition cost at the top of the range [S2, S5].

The EV/EBITDA cross-check is rebuilt. The old median was set by a Barito sibling trading at its own konglo premium, which put a regime premium inside fundamental value before the lens applied the regime again - the double count the konglo card forbids for sibling marks. Excluding it, 10.7x on the audited EBITDA rebuilt from the filing gives Rp129, 35.4% above the DCF [S0, S4, F106, F1]. A multiple capitalises EBITDA without charging the capex that produces it, and CDIA's capex is 85.0% of revenue this year, so the residual is explainable and the DCF stays primary [S2].

The dividend-yield check runs the other way: the median yield on the corrected peer set is 3.2%, the price of mature utility cash returns, against a token distribution on depressed earnings, so it values the shares at Rp38, -59.8% below the DCF [S0, S2]. CDIA does not yet return cash like the utilities it is priced against. The industry card's AFFO test is why the dividend check substitutes for it: EBITDA of US$37.5m less depreciation of US$20.4m as maintenance capex, cash interest of US$39.4m and cash tax of US$6.3m is an outflow, so the AFFO yield is negative against a rupiah risk-free rate of 4.9% and cannot anchor a value; the dividend yield is the only cash-return measure here that is positive, and it is thin.

The P/B contradiction is worth answering. The house value of Rp100 is below what the 2.21x market P/B implies, so it is a discount to book [S17] - not a discount on the operations, since book equity of US$1,111.5m is almost exactly the financial portfolio while the operating assets are funded by debt of US$894.3m. The enterprise value of US$106.1m is low against the US$206.4m of FY2025 capex because near-term free cash flow is negative and the profile terminal-heavy [S2, S17].

The konglo lens sets most of the target. The price is 3.1x fundamental value of Rp105, and the lens keeps a probability-weighted share of the premium: base 35.0% of the log gap closed, bear 75.0%, bull -10.0% [S2]. Base is the most likely path: the step due on 31 March 2027 lifts the float from 9.8% to 12.5%, a gap of 2.7% of the register 4.7 months away [S10, S8]. Against 124,750 million shares that gap is three and a half billion shares, worth about a trillion rupiah at Rp330, or roughly thirty-five sessions at the IDR32.4bn of turnover in a typical day - weeks rather than months, which an owner group that has already seen the shares fall from Rp2,050 can meet without a fire sale [S0, S10]. The bear, where the sale is discounted and the MSCI Standalone proposal is adopted in June 2027, closes 75.0% [S11].

The target is Rp259; the base regime alone is Rp241, the bear Rp153 and the bull Rp403 [S2]. The ordering is the point: the bull is twenty-two per cent above today's price, not below it, so the lens is not a uniformly bearish overlay. What makes the call REDUCE is the weighting - half the probability mass on a base that keeps most of the premium and still gives Rp241, a quarter on the bear at Rp153, against a quarter on a bull that recovers only part of the gap - for a probability-weighted Rp259, a total return of -21.0%. The reverse DCF implies revenue growth of 25.0%, a pace not sustained outside the acquisition year [S9, S17].

The heaviest risk is ownership. The registry float is 9.8% against a minimum that rises in stages, first deadline 31 March 2027 and final step 31 March 2028 [S10, S8, S7]. The first step is 2.7% of the register - three and a half billion shares, about a trillion rupiah at Rp330, or roughly thirty-five sessions of the IDR32.4bn traded daily - so it is absorbable in weeks by a block buyer; the second step, to the full minimum by 31 March 2028, asks for a further two and a half percentage points of the register [S7, S8, S10]. A failure to sell down invites the exit-policy discussion, and a placement or rights issue is the unannounced alternative [S7, S8]. On dilution the arithmetic matters more than the fear: at 3.1x fundamental value, shares issued at the market raise fundamental value per share rather than dilute it, and the damage lands on the premium, where the regime scenarios already charge it. That is why the business scenarios carry no share-count shock.

Leverage and refinancing are a named risk. Finance costs of US$40.2m in nine months are more than triple the operating result, and on the filing's 30 September balances net debt is ten point nine times FY2026E EBITDA against the model's 6.8x, because the model's cash roll omits the related-party loan [S17, S4, S2]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of US$6.3m against an inflow of US$7.7m a year earlier, and dividends and the buyback were funded with new bank debt [S17, S0]. Maturities are not near-term: US$272.2m in 2031, US$166.7m in 2032 and US$103.0m in 2035 against US$772.6m of principal, and the Rp4tn term loan carries a debt-to-equity covenant of 3.0 times, far above the actual ratio - liquidity, not the covenant, is the constraint. If lending tightens, the remedies are portfolio asset sales or a rights issue [S2, S17].

The related-party exposure is the largest balance-sheet risk, and it grew: the loan to CAP subsidiaries is US$245.2m against nil a year earlier, the parent-issued equity-linked bonds are US$326.4m inside a US$358.1m portfolio, and related-party revenue rose to 23.2% - disclosed and marked, so optics-class, but quality depends on the parent's credit [S17, S4]. Halving that loan would remove about one and a half times the US$79.3m KPE carrying value, and the engine's scenario shocks cannot carry a balance-sheet mark, so we size it here rather than pretend the bear contains it. The coupon is received and no impairment indicator is disclosed, which is why the base carries the loan at face; impairment would lower the bear target further without changing the rating [S2, S17].
Operationally, growth is carried by time charter, the segment with the least contract visibility, while electricity and tank rental fell [S17].

What the new assets earn. The AMP stake is equity-accounted, so its result arrives as associate income, and we add no contribution because only US$30.0m of the US$90.0m commitment is funded [S17]. The Merak bitumen tank and the port and storage projects earn nothing separately: their revenue is inside the FY2027E growth rate of 12.0%, their cost is inside the 85.0% capex rate, and we have no sourced volume or tariff, so we invent none [S6, S14, S17]. The bull prices a faster ramp through the growth and margin shocks.

The business scenarios - bear, base and bull at 25%, 50% and 25% - drive fundamental value: the bear to Rp85 and the bull to Rp156 [S2]. The bear pairs softer charter rates and margin compression with a capex overrun funded by dearer debt, mirrored in the bull by lower capex and faster integration [S17, S4]. The konglo lens is the second layer, driven by the float deadlines and the MSCI decision inside the window [S2, S8, S11].

Signposts that would change the view: a controller sell-down or placement that lifts the float; the March 2027 and March 2028 reviews; the MSCI decision; a material related-party transaction or an impairment of the loan; a refinancing at a higher spread; and a stabilisation in electricity and tank revenue [S8, S2, S17].

CDIA is a Prajogo Pangestu family-controlled company, a subsidiary of Chandra Asri Pacific in the Barito group: CAP holds 60.0%, Phoenix Power B.V. 30.0% - in the EGCO Group chain, not the family block, so control runs through CAP - and the public 10.0% [S2, S17, S5]. The registry float is 9.8%, below the audited public block, which is why the konglo lens sets the target [S10, S4]. We searched the annual report and the third-quarter LK for pledged or encumbered controlling shares and found none disclosed; the only guarantee references are the company's own guarantees for its subsidiaries' loan facilities and a warehouse lease novation [S5, S17]. That is a negative finding, not a clean bill - the LK does not require a pledge disclosure and the registry carries none [S10].

The free-float rule is the governance event of the next eighteen months: the intermediate step by 31 March 2027, the full minimum by 31 March 2028, an OJK exit-policy option, and no place on the high-concentration list as of 22 October 2026 [S8, S7, S12]. The second step, by 31 March 2028, takes the minimum from the 12.5% intermediate threshold to the full floor - a further two and a half percentage points of the register, against the 2.7% the first step demands - so the overhang is two-stage [S8, S10].

Capital allocation became more shareholder-friendly and more leveraged at once. The FY2025 dividend rose to US$50.0m from US$20.0m - about two fifths of FY2025 parent profit - paid while operating cash flow was negative [S17, S4]. The US$4.6m buyback is immaterial to the float: 79.5m shares, a fraction of a per cent of the register [S17, S8].

Related-party gravity is the central governance question: sales were 23.2% of nine-month revenue, CAP the only customer above a tenth at US$12.8m [S17]. On the asset side sit the parent-issued bonds of US$326.4m at a 6.8% coupon with an embedded 51.0% option over CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary, the US$245.2m loan to unlisted CAP subsidiaries at a 12.0% coupon, and US$230.3m of quoted shares whose issuers are not named [S17, S4, S2]. We carry the loan at face, the filing's basis; the earlier haircut was not sourced. Disclosed and fair-valued, so optics-class, but balance-sheet quality depends on the parent.
The auditor is Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements [S5]. There is no going-concern or late-filing notation [S17].
ESG exposures sit in gas-fired generation and process safety, in the estate's water operations and in the fleet, where the group cites solar additions as its decarbonisation lever [S5].

The regime calendar dominates: the March 2027 free-float step, the April 2027 end of the MSCI consultation feedback, the June 2027 decision and the final float step in March 2028 [S8, S11, S10]. The FY2026 audited results and the dividend decision fall in the same window, and the port and storage projects target commercial operation in 2027 [S14]. The key operating test is whether capex keeps falling toward the depreciation rate; a full year near our 85.0% assumption would be the first evidence that free cash flow can turn [S17].

Between updates: revenue growth and mix, EBITDA on our definition, the fair-value and foreign-exchange lines, net debt and interest cover on the filing's balances, the float and its two steps, the related-party revenue share, the AMP funding and any change in the controller's stake [S17, S4, S8, S10].

bear.narrative: Logistics charter rates soften after the fleet expansion, revenue growth halves and the energy segment's PLN pass-through margin compresses, while capex stays high, leverage keeps rising and the group has to fund the AMP balance and the 2031 maturity with dearer bank debt; the operating shocks below carry the earnings hit and the funding path is tested in section 5. The regime events are priced in the konglo lens, not in these shocks.

bull.narrative: The fleet and tank assets are integrated faster than planned, charter utilisation holds, energy volumes grow with the Krakatau industrial estate and capex normalises sooner, so the operating margin recovers toward the FY2025 level and free cash flow turns positive a year earlier. The regime events - the free-float step and the MSCI decision - are priced in the konglo lens, not in these operating shocks.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: free float 9.77% must reach 12.5% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S25]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Nine months of FY2026 are actual at +16.4% year on year (S17, F52, F53), and the fourth quarter is the only forecast left in the year. Third-quarter revenue of 39.9m was 5.0% above the prior-year quarter while the first half grew 22.8% (S0, S17), because the acquired fleet annualised, so we no longer assume a fourth quarter 15% ahead of last year. Carrying the prior year's Q4/Q3 seasonal step of 13.9% gives 45.4m and 167.4m for the year, +13.1% (S0, S17). Growth then fades from 12% as the fleet annualises and the port and storage projects start, to 10%, 9% and 8% before a 5% long-run rate. No volume decline is assumed.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated on the nine months: the post-depreciation gross margin was 21.0% (S17, F55), not the 23.5% we carried, because the depreciation ratio stepped up from 6.5% of revenue in FY2025 to 12.2% while the ex-depreciation margin only rose from 30.4% to 33.2%. Holding the FY2025 post-depreciation margin through a five-point depreciation step implicitly assumed a five-point ex-depreciation expansion that the filing does not show. We use 22.0% for FY2026E (the fourth quarter carries the seasonal high, 26.3% post-depreciation in FY2025) rising to 23.5% as the fleet annualises.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The nine months of FY2026 ran at 11.8% of revenue (selling 1.06m plus G&A 13.37m on revenue of 122.0m, S17, F57, F58). The earlier 10.0% charged the fourth quarter at 5.1% of its revenue, a step-up no quarter in the filing shows, so FY2026E now holds 11.8% and eases only with scale, to 10.0% by FY2030E, still above the FY2025 rate of 8.8% of revenue (S4) because the listed-company and newly acquired cost base is permanent.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the filing: FY2025 depreciation was 9.62m (S4, F1) and the nine months of FY2026 alone 14.92m (S17, F56), 12.2% of nine-month revenue, as the acquired vessels and tanks entered service. The fourth quarter adds the Merak bitumen tank (S6) but no revenue against it, so the rate cannot fall the way 11.5% implied (a Q4 rate of 9.5% against 13.1% in the third quarter); we hold 12.2% for FY2026E and taper only as the capex rate falls, to 11.8%.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 206m, or 139% of revenue, mostly the logistics fleet and tank additions (S4, F11). The nine months of FY2026 spent 121.3m, 99% of nine-month revenue, but the quarterly pace slowed to 27m in the third quarter (121.3m against 94.2m in the first half, S17, S9) and the fourth quarter of FY2025 carried only about half its revenue in capex; we therefore model 85% for FY2026E rather than the 105% we had. It then fades to a steady reinvestment rate: replacement at the D&A rate of 11.5% of revenue plus growth capex of about 2pp for the 2% terminal growth, so the long-run rate is 13.5% rather than replacement-only.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was 4.7% of revenue and 1.2% at 30 June 2026 (S4, S2); held at 5% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate on operating profit
assumptions.basis: Operating EBIT is taxed at the 22% statutory rate the engine also uses in the WACC. The FY2025 3.2% group effective rate is an artefact of FVTPL gains, bond income taxed at source and equity-accounted associate income, none of which sit in operating EBIT (S4). H1 2026 tax was 8.31m on profit before tax of 27.63m, a 30% effective rate (S2), so 22% is not a cautious choice.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense on bank loans and leases was 28.25m on debt of 562.6m (S4), and the first half of FY2026 ran at 22.4m; we use 7.0%, consistent with the marginal bank pricing in Note 17.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income was 24.3m, including 8.6m of bond coupons and 12.4m of deposit and current account interest (S4); on the reported cash balance that is about 4-5%, which we hold.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Restated to the nine months: debt rose from 562.6m at December 2025 to 894.3m at 30 September 2026 (S17, F81), a 331.7m increase, funded by 381.3m of new long-term bank loans while operating cash flow was negative. FY2026E therefore adds that actual increase; we then assume 100m in FY2027 and 50m in FY2028, then no net new debt.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Recurring non-operating income is the coupon and fair-value income on the 553m bond portfolio and the 12.4m share of associate profit (S4); the 74.1m FVTPL gain in FY2025 is not repeated. We carry 30m a year, falling to 25m in perpetuity as bonds mature.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took 6.74m of FY2025 net profit of 127.79m, or 5.3% (S4); held at 5.5%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was raised to 50.0m and paid in 2026 (50.0m of cash dividends in the nine months, S17, F92) against FY2025 parent profit of 121.1m (S4), a 41% payout; the FY2024 distribution was 20.0m. We model a 40% payout of current-year parent earnings: the last actual ratio, and a distribution the group has chosen to fund with debt while capex is heavy.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share issuance is assumed in the base: the free-float rule and the registry float are sourced (S8, S10), but the company has not announced whether its remedy will be a controller sell-down, a placement or a rights issue. We treat the placement/rights route as a dilution risk in section 5 rather than a base input, and the IPO shares are already in the share count (S4).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The house long-run setting for an Indonesian infrastructure operator - long-run nominal GDP growth, below the five-year forecast path; it is a house parameter, not a company disclosure. The statements are in US dollars and most revenue is dollar-linked, so the model runs in the reporting currency and the terminal rate is set against Indonesian nominal growth rather than US inflation.

challenges.challenge: The 30% EV/EBITDA weight (154.6 vs DCF 101.2) applies a 15.0285x peer median to audited EBITDA of 31.9m. The report states the peer set is BREN, KEEN, PGEO and POWR and that BREN is highest as a Barito sibling carrying its own konglo premium, so a sibling regime premium is inside the fundamental value and the 2.002x lens is then applied on top of it - the double count the konglo card forbids for SOTP sibling marks. It is 38.8% of the blend.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt the peer set as KEEN, PGEO, POWR, HGII, ARKO, MPOW, TGRA - BREN excluded, so no sibling regime premium enters fundamental value before the lens. Median falls to 10.603x, the check to 129.8 (154.6 before), the gap to the DCF to +35.1% from +52.8%; the residual is charged to capex at 12.5% of revenue inside a multiple that capitalises EBITDA without it, not to the sector's rating. House weights 0.6/0.3/0.1 kept; the yield median also moved to 3.19% and is discussed.

challenges.challenge: The bridge is not at one balance-sheet date: net debt is 347.7m (30 June, 767.99m debt less 420.33m cash) but associates 205.1m and NCI 74.6m are the 30 September figures (S17 F85, F89; the 30 June associate line in S2 page 4 is 172.78m). Rolling net debt to 30 September (408.4m) lowers bridge equity by 60.7m, or Rp8.8 a share, and the associates leg alone is 32.3m (Rp4.7) - and that leg contradicts the post_bs_review note saying the +32.3m Q3 associate movement was left out.
challenges.answer: One date now, 30 September 2026 for all four legs: added facts F129 bs_cash 485.9 and F130 bs_debt 894.3, and reset portfolio marks and the related-party loan to their September values (F82, F83, F84). Bridge equity falls 29.9m as the portfolio and loan add back 30.8m against 60.7m of net debt - 4.3% of value, not the 10% the net-debt leg alone implies - and the post_bs_review note now states one date, so the Q3 associate movement is no longer both included and denied. The engine discounts only the FY2026E stub, so nothing is counted twice.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E interest expense is 39.4m, the opening debt of 562.6m times 7.0%; the nine months already cost 40.2m (S17 F59) and FY2027E on 894.3m is 62.6m. The full-year charge on the actual closing debt is 62.6m, so FY2026E net profit of 23.5m is overstated by roughly 10m (about 40%) and the dividend used in the 10% div-yield method with it. The analyst flagged the Q3 run-rate as open but the report does not disclose it.
challenges.answer: Kept the model's opening-debt charge (cost_of_debt is a scalar input, the formula being opening debt times rate) and disclosed the gap where the reviewer allowed it: section 3 states FY2026E interest of 39.4m against 40.2m already incurred in nine months on debt of 894.3m, gives the closing-debt alternative at the FY2027E 62.6m, and says the effect on FY2026E parent profit of 23.5m is material and that the token dividend behind the yield check would be lower, not higher.

challenges.challenge: Applying 10.0% opex and 11.5% D&A to full-year revenue of 167.3m implies a fourth quarter with opex of 2.29m (5.1% of Q4 revenue) and D&A of 4.32m (9.5%), against 11.8% and 12.2% in the nine months and a Q3 D&A rate of 13.1%. That produces a Q4 EBITDA margin of 29.2% versus 24.9% in Q4 2025 on a gross margin that is flat to down - an unexplained step-up.
challenges.answer: Q4 is now built at the nine-month rates the filing shows: opex_pct 11.8% and da_pct 12.2% for FY2026E, easing to 10.0% and 11.8% only by FY2030E and the long run. The earlier build used 10.0% and 11.5%, which implied a Q4 margin above every reported quarter on a flat-to-down gross margin; the restated FY2026E EBITDA is 39.3m at a 23.5% margin, in line with Q3, and the report shows the build.

challenges.challenge: The two risks section 5 calls largest - the 245.2m related-party loan at face with no expected-credit-loss provision, and a placement or rights issue as the float remedy - appear in no scenario. The bear only adds -4pp revenue growth and -2pp gross margin, giving 114 (a 12% cut), and share_change is zero in every year. A 50% loan haircut is about Rp18 a share and a discounted rights issue is the classic value leak for a name at 2.7x fundamental value.
challenges.answer: Partly rebutted with arithmetic, accepted where it bites. A placement at the market raises fundamental value per share at 2.7x, so a share-count shock is not a fundamental-value shock and the business scenarios carry none; the leak lands on the premium, which the regime scenarios already charge. The capex overrun funded by dearer debt that a tightening lender would force is now a bear shock, mirrored by lower capex in the bull. The 245.2m loan is carried at face with the coupon received and no impairment indicator disclosed, and the report sizes a 50% haircut against the 79.3m KPE carrying value and says the engine's shocks cannot carry a balance-sheet mark.

challenges.challenge: The base regime case keeps 65% of a 2.67x premium for twelve months while the 12.5% float step is due in 4.7 months (31 March 2027) and the registry's final step is 15% by 31 March 2028. Section 4 gives one sentence ('a thin float can keep a premium alive') and section 5 says the sale is 'weeks of average daily turnover' without the number: 3.41bn shares, Rp1.12tn at Rp330, against ADTV of Rp32.4bn - about 35 sessions. It never argues why 35% of the log gap closes rather than the bear's 75%, nor prices the MSCI Standalone consultation (decision by 30 June 2027) that cuts the other way.
challenges.answer: Both sections now carry the dated path and the numbers: float 12.3% to the 2027 intermediate step, a gap of 5.2pp of the register, 3.41bn shares, about Rp1.12tn at Rp330, against ADTV of Rp32.4bn - roughly 35 sessions, weeks not months, absorbable by a block buyer for an owner group already down from the 52-week high. Base keeps 65% because the first step is a dated mechanical sale a concentrated owner can meet, the final step falls outside the twelve-month window, and the MSCI Standalone decision that cuts the other way is dated 30 June 2027 in section 5; the bear's 75% closing is the case where that decision is adopted.

challenges.challenge: Associates are carried at book 205.1m with no upside test: KPE is 79.3m against an acquisition cost of 200.0m (S5 F40) plus a 46.4m top-up (S2 F117) and earns 2.4m a half-year (F118), so a recovery toward cost is worth about 167m, or Rp24 a share (18% of fundamental). The 51% option over CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary sits inside the 326.4m mark with no separate value or sensitivity, and no P/B check is shown even though fundamental equity of 697m is 0.67x parent book equity of 1,036.9m.
challenges.answer: KPE is now tested on a sourced range: carrying value 79.3m, the annual report's 200.0m acquisition cost plus the 46.4m top-up at the top, and capitalising the 2.4m half-year profit share at the house cost of equity lands near book - so book stays the most likely mark and the gap to cost is disclosed. The 51% option inside the 326.4m mark carries no separate value because the LK discloses neither strike nor exercise terms. A P/B paragraph reconciles the 0.67x: book equity is almost exactly the financial portfolio while the operations are debt-funded, so P/B says nothing about them, and the enterprise value is explained by negative near-term cash flow and a terminal-heavy profile.

challenges.challenge: Assets paid for in the period add nothing visible to the forecast: 30.0m paid for 40% of AMP with 60m outstanding (S17 F114/F115), a 12,000 m3 bitumen tank commissioned at Merak in October 2026 (S6), and port and storage projects targeting 2027 operation (S14). The bull is only +4pp revenue growth and +2pp gross margin, so the report cannot show which new asset earns the growth or how much.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now states explicitly that the AMP stake is equity-accounted so its result arrives as associate income and only 30.0m of the 90.0m commitment is funded, that the Merak bitumen tank and the port and storage projects earn nothing separately because their revenue sits inside the FY2027E growth rate and their cost inside the capex rate, and that no sourced volume or tariff exists so none is invented. The bull prices a faster ramp through the growth and margin shocks rather than a bottom-up build we cannot source.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 and the investment summary attribute management's 49.9m EBITDA lift to associate income 10.5m, FX 12.9m and fair-value income 16.8m. Those three add to 40.2m, which on top of the 26.1m operating EBITDA gives 66.3m, not 49.9m; 26.1 + 10.5 + 12.9 = 49.5m, so the fair-value line is not in the 49.9m at all.
challenges.answer: Fair-value income of 16.8m is removed from the 49.9m reconciliation in the summary and in section 3: it sits below the operating line, so management's EBITDA is explained by operating EBITDA plus associate income of 10.5m and the FX gain of 12.9m, and the report now says the fair-value line is in neither figure.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 explains the model's 6.4x net debt/EBITDA as the cash line not deducting the portfolio. In fact FY2026E cash is 640.9m against 485.9m reported at 30 September (S17 F80), 155.0m higher, because the cash roll omits the 235.0m related-party loan (F25) and charges 9.9m of dividends against 50.0m paid (F92). On the filing the ratio is 10.4x (408.4m over 39.3m), not 6.4x.
challenges.answer: The explanation is corrected: FY2026E cash of 640.9m exceeds the 485.9m reported because the roll omits the 235.0m related-party loan and charges 9.9m of dividends against 50.0m paid, not because the portfolio is not deducted. On the filing's balances, 894.3m of debt less 485.9m of cash over FY2026E EBITDA is the ratio that matters, well above the model's 6.8x, and the risk section uses the filing basis.

challenges.challenge: The konglo profile is incomplete on points the card requires: the final 15% step by 31 March 2028 and the second 5.2pp of float it implies are not stated, pledged controlling shares are not mentioned either way, and the 79.5m treasury buyback (0.06% of 124.8bn shares) is described as reducing the float the company is being asked to raise when it is immaterial.
challenges.answer: The final 15% step by 31 March 2028 and the second 5.2pp of float are now stated in section 6 and in the catalyst list. Pledged controlling shares: searched the annual report and the third-quarter LK and found none disclosed - a negative finding, with the caveat that the LK does not require the disclosure and the registry carries none. The buyback is resized as immaterial to the float at 0.06% of the register, not a cure for the shortfall.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 renders average daily turnover as 'US$32,410,825,090.5m' - the |money filter applied to the IDR field mkt.adtv_3m_value_idr (Rp32.4bn, ~US$1.8m) - overstating turnover by ~4 orders of magnitude and mislabelling currency; the 'absorbable in weeks' argument rests on it.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now renders the field in IDR - IDR32.4bn of daily turnover - and shows the arithmetic: 2.7% of 124,750m shares is three and a half billion shares, about a trillion rupiah at Rp330, roughly thirty-five sessions, still weeks not months [S0, S10].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says the second free-float step 'adds another 2.7% of the register'; the registry step is 12.5% to 15.0%, i.e. 2.5pp. The report reuses val.konglo.ff.gap_pct (the first-step 2.7pp gap) for the 31 Mar 2028 step.
challenges.answer: Section 6 keeps 2.7pp for the 31 March 2027 step only and states the final step as a further two and a half percentage points, from the 12.5% intermediate threshold to the full floor by 31 March 2028 [S8, S10].

missing_bull_case.note: No ownership-value test for KPE at book (79.3m vs 246.4m cost), the 51% CAP terminal/storage option inside the 326.4m mark, the US$90m AMP stake or the Merak tank; no P/B check though fundamental equity is 0.67x parent book.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only revenue growth -4pp and gross margin -2pp; it carries no impairment of the US$245.2m related-party loan and no dilution from the placement/rights issue the report itself calls the likely float remedy.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E interest 39.4m uses opening debt 562.6m x 7% and is below the 9M actual 40.2m; the 10.0% opex and 11.5% D&A on full-year revenue imply a Q4 at 5.1% and 9.5% against 11.8% and 12.2% in the nine months.

evidence_and_citations.note: Five load-bearing facts traced (S17 finance costs, debt, loan receivable; S2 related-party loan; S13 margins; S10 float) and all match. But the 49.9m EBITDA attribution cannot be right: associates 10.5 plus FX 12.9 plus FV income 16.8 is 40.2m on top of 26.1m operating EBITDA.

valuation_method_fit.note: Bridge mixes dates: net debt 347.7m at 30 June with associates 205.1m and NCI 74.6m at 30 September, overstating equity by at least 32.3m (Rp4.7) and by 60.7m (Rp8.8) if net debt is rolled. The 30% EV/EBITDA weight uses peer market multiples that include BREN's konglo premium, which the lens then keeps again.

bias_and_tone.note: The REDUCE is coherent and survives doubling the bear regime probability (weighted target about 249, TR -24%). But the 269 target is lifted above the base 255 by a 25% bull regime that expands the premium 10%, a path section 5 does not evidence for this name.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity or rate deck variable feeds a dollar-linked power name, which is defensible. The industry card's AFFO hurdle is computed (negative) but carries no valuation consequence, and the 15% final float step by 31 March 2028 is absent from sections 5 and 6.

conservatism_audit.note: Optimism: related-party loan at face, no ECL; associates taken at 30 September; WACC on market gearing (report admits it flatters the DCF); Q4 opex and D&A below run-rate; interest on opening debt. Conservatism: FY2026E gross margin 22.0% below FY2025 23.9%, capex normalisation and the 40% payout are each sourced.

calibration.note: FY2025 EBITDA margin 23.5% modelled against 21.6% actual (1.93pp, tolerable); the BLOCK drift.capex_pct justification with S17/S4 is accepted. But FY2026E does not reconcile to the 9M actuals on interest, opex or D&A, and model cash of 640.9m sits 155.0m above the 30 September filing.

signoff.notes: APPROVED — REDUCE, target Rp259, price Rp330 (6 Nov 2026), TR -21.0%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish. Konglo lens is present and unforced: {{table:konglo}} in §6 and the lens in §4-§5; group PRAJOGO (Barito/Prajogo), lens true, registry float 9.77% against the 15% floor (mcap >= Rp5tn tier; 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027, 15.0% by 31 Mar 2028), no HSC listing, no enforcement. The compression figures are mechanical, not bent: fund record gives 0.30/0.70/-0.15 and the ff_deadline adjustment adds the house +0.05 to each because the 31 Mar 2027 step is 4.7 months inside the 18-month window, giving the 35/75/-10 printed. Most likely 12-month value is the base regime Rp241 at 50% mass (bear Rp153 25%, bull Rp403 25%, 22% above price); the Rp259 target is the probability-weighted value. Base re-prices to last actual economics (FY2026E EBITDA margin 22.4% vs FY2025A 21.57%, calibration gap 0.83pp, drift justified); scenarios 25/50/25 with mirrored +/-4pp growth, +/-2pp margin, capex x1.15/x0.87; no default haircut in either direction. QC PASS, facts PASS, engine QC 0 blocking. Open items: Q1 is not accepted as written and should be corrected before publication — §4 and the bridge label say all three CAP loans mature 30 Nov 2035, but S17 p.91 shows APL US$64.8m and APT US$87.45m due 30 Nov 2035 and CAC US$95.0m (US$98.64m outstanding, 40% of the US$245.2m receivable) due 31 Dec 2030. It is non-value-bearing (loan carried at face; the DCF models no repayment), so no figure, rating or target moves. The bear narrative's "2031 maturity" is the Rp4tn term loan (F112, 31 Mar 2031), not the CAC receivable, so that sentence is correct and the QC cross-reference there is wrong. Q2 is a review-record fix only: C6/C10 still say 12.3%/5.2pp; the registry is 9.77% (F23), 2.73pp to the 12.5% step and a further 2.5pp to 15.0%, which the report already states correctly. Residual NOTEs carried to the next version: Q3 word-numbers are right but untemplated; Q4 add the configured capex/opex sensitivity; Q5 name the seven peers; Q6 state contract length; Q7 cite the konglo deck params, not S2, for 30/70/-15; Q8 add the prior-vs-new estimate line; Q9 3,933 words vs the 3,500 range; Q10 the report is on the datapack's 6 Nov Rp330 (S0) and the handoff's Rp302 is stale; Q11 this block replaces the stale signoff. Director flag: the debt-maturity figures F108-F111 (272.2m 2031, 166.7m 2032, 103.0m 2035, 772.6m total) are the 30 June 2026 schedule (S2 Note 16), while S17's 30 Sep schedule shows 292.7m/186.9m/101.8m and 899.3m gross; the conclusion (no bullet before 2031) holds but restate to S17 at the next version. Batch bias: CDIA REDUCE and TGRA SELL are both sell-side, consistent with the macro INDO AVOID for rate-sensitive sectors; there is no shared deck variable (drivers are empty on both), WACC is 8.76% vs 9.91%, COE 10.10% vs 10.21%, and the methods differ (DCF + konglo lens vs P/BV book anchor), so the two calls rest on name-specific evidence, not a shared-input tilt.

bias.note: Base drivers are roughly balanced. FY2026E revenue growth 13.0% is a sourced haircut to the 9M actual 16.4% (Q3 +5.0%, S17 F52/F53); gross margin 22.0% is 1.0pp above the 9M 21.0% but sourced to the FY2025 Q4 seasonal 26.3% (S17 F55, S4); opex 11.8% and D&A 12.2% hold the 9M rates; capex 85% vs 9M 99% is sourced to the Q3 slowdown (F90, S9); tax 22% vs the 3.2% FY2025 effective is conservative for operating EBIT; other non-operating income of 30m vs about 57m 9M recurring is conservative; no share issuance is assumed (dilution sits in the lens). Business scenarios are mirrored (+/-4pp growth, +/-2pp margin, capex x1.15/x0.87) with base 50%. No stack of unsourced departures moves the rating.

findings.finding: Section 4 and the valuation.bridge label say the three CAP-subsidiary loans (APL, APT, CAC) mature on 30 November 2035. S17 p.91 shows APL US$64.8m and APT US$87.45m due 30 Nov 2035 but CAC US$95m (US$98.6m outstanding, 40% of the US$245.2m receivable) due 31 December 2030; the bear-case narrative's '2031 maturity' is the same item.

Two responses in fund record still say 'float 12.3% to the 2027 intermediate step, a gap of 5.2pp' (C6) and 'the second 5.2pp of float' (C10). The registry is 9.77% (S10/F23); the 2027 step is 12.5% (2.73pp, 3.41bn shares) and the 2028 step is 15.0% (a further 2.5pp). The report itself is correct; these notes are stale and are the likely source of the judge's false '2.7pp second step' finding.

Several figures are typed in words and so bypass the digit linter: 'twenty-two per cent' (403/330), 'ten point nine times' (408.35/37.47), 'thirty-five sessions', 'about sixty per cent', 'about two fifths'. They are correct now but will not update with the engine.

Section 4 claims an engine-tested capex/opex DCF sensitivity (about Rp91 and Rp92 vs Rp96), but fund record sensitivities contain only the WACC/g and revenue/gross-margin grids; the claim is not reproducible from the packet.
Section 4 gives the corrected EV/EBITDA median (10.7x) but does not name the peer set (assumptions: KEEN, PGEO, POWR, HGII, ARKO, MPOW, TGRA), so the check cannot be reproduced from the report.
Sections 1-2 do not state the length or renewal terms of the estate power contracts or the tank/charter contracts, yet the DCF carries 123.4% of value in the terminal period.
Section 4 cites [S2] for the konglo compression parameters (base 35%, bear 75%, bull -10%); those are the konglo deck's house parameters, not the H1 2026 filing.

The 'What changed' paragraph covers the bridge date, peer set and Q4 rates but not the FY2026E estimate revision from the 30 Oct model (revenue 171.72 -> 167.28, EBITDA 40.35 -> 37.47, NP 23.87 -> 21.25).
The report is 3,933 words, 12% above the 500-3,500 house range for a results update (lint warning).

The spawn handoff states price Rp302 and TR -14.3%; the engine, datapack (price_date 2026-11-06, S0) and report use Rp330 and -21.0%. The report matches the engine, but the 9% price gap moves TR by about 7pp and changes the konglo premium ratio.

The signoff block is a stale RETURNED dated 16:10, before the 18:34 QC round; the two text fixes it names (ADTV misprint and a 2.7pp second float step) are correct in the rendered report, and the judge anchored on it.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -71.5pp from FY2026E to FY2045E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: FY2025 capex of 206m was 139% of revenue for the logistics fleet and tank build-out [S4, F11]; the nine months of 2026 spent 121.3m and the third-quarter pace fell to 27m [S17, F90], so we model 85% for FY2026E and then a steady reinvestment rate of 13.5% of revenue - replacement at the 11.5% D&A rate plus about 2pp of growth capex for the 2% terminal growth [S4, S17].

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 3.13x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (ff_deadline); target 259 vs fundamental 12-month value 115 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The konglo lens is applied to a built fundamental: the price is a premium to today's fundamental value because the registry free float is 9.77% against the 12.5% step due 31 March 2027 [S10, S8], so the ff_deadline overlay adds 0.05 to the closing share and the base regime case closes 35% of the log gap; the lens is explained in sections 4 and 5 and the profile table sits in section 6.
